These papers tackle the core challenge of aligning AI models with human values and intentions—training systems to follow our goals accurately and honestly without cutting corners or gaming the system.

Learning what humans actually prefer

75

Training AI systems to match human preferences by collecting feedback on model outputs and adjusting the system to produce what people actually want.

ICLR 2026

PALC: Preference Alignment via Logit Calibration

Problem. Aligning LLMs with human preferences typically requires computationally intensive training or complex reward architectures.
Approach. We introduce PALC (Preference Alignment via Logit Calibration), a parameter-efficient framework operating at the logit layer where each dimension corresponds to a token, using a bottleneck architecture to learn position-dependent calibration vectors.
Contribution. PALC outperforms most test-time alignment methods while maintaining near-baseline inference speed and enabling runtime adjustment of alignment strength without retraining.

Towards Safe Reasoning in Large Reasoning Models via Corrective Intervention

Problem. Large reasoning models' chain-of-thought reasoning often contains harmful content that persists even when final responses appear safe, undermining trustworthiness.
Approach. Proposes Intervened Preference Optimization using process supervision, substituting compliance steps with safety triggers and constructing preference pairs with strong signals for safe reasoning.
Contribution. Remarkably improves overall safety regarding both reasoning and responses, with >30% relative reduction in harmful content over SFT and RL baselines.
process supervisionpreference optimizationsafety intervention

Eliminating Inductive Bias in Reward Models with Information-Theoretic Guidance

Problem. Reward models in RLHF contain preference conflicts and inductive biases like response length and speaking style, leading to reward overfitting.
Approach. Proposes DIR (Debiasing via Information optimization for RM), maximizing mutual information between predictions and responses while minimizing MI with biased attributes.
Contribution. Effectively diminishes multiple types of inductive bias and improves RLHF performance across benchmarks with better generalization abilities.

Alignment through Meta-Weighted Online Sampling: Bridging the Gap between Data Generation and Preference Optimization

Problem. Distribution mismatch between pre-collected offline preference data and evolving model policy limits alignment effectiveness; existing methods fail to adapt to model's dynamic learning state.
Approach. MetaAPO couples data generation with training via a lightweight meta-learner that evaluates online sampling benefits and assigns sample-wise meta-weights balancing online and offline data quality.
Contribution. Consistently outperforms preference optimization baselines on AlpacaEval 2, Arena-Hard, and MT-Bench while reducing online annotation costs by 42%.

Reinforcement Unlearning via Group Relative Policy Optimization

Problem. LLMs memorize sensitive data during pretraining, creating compliance risks under GDPR and EU AI Act, and existing unlearning methods leak data, sacrifice fluency, or require expensive reward models.
Approach. PURGE uses Group Relative Policy Optimization with an intrinsic reward penalizing forbidden concepts, enabling safe unlearning without external reward models.
Contribution. PURGE achieves up to 46x lower token usage than state-of-the-art, improves fluency by +5.48% and robustness by +12.02%, reaching 11% unlearning effectiveness while preserving 98% utility.

Beyond RLHF and NLHF: Population-Proportional Alignment under an Axiomatic Framework

Problem. Conventional preference learning aggregates preferences from multiple evaluators but may result in policies biased toward majority opinions and susceptible to strategic manipulation.
Approach. The paper develops a novel framework grounded in social choice theory that infers feasible evaluator population distributions from pairwise comparison data and constructs policies satisfying foundational axioms.
Contribution. The framework aligns policies proportionally with true population preferences while satisfying monotonicity, Pareto efficiency, population-proportional alignment, and bounded manipulability axioms.

Uni-DPO: A Unified Paradigm for Dynamic Preference Optimization of LLMs

Problem. Existing DPO-based methods treat all preference pairs equally, overlooking substantial variations in data quality and learning difficulty, leading to inefficient data utilization.
Approach. Uni-DPO adaptively reweights samples based on both the inherent quality of preference pairs and the model's evolving performance during training.
Contribution. Gemma-2-9B-IT fine-tuned with Uni-DPO surpasses Claude 3 Opus by 6.7 points on Arena-Hard, with consistent outperformance across mathematical and multimodal tasks.

Problem. LLM alignment faces imbalanced safety datasets overrepresenting common hazards while neglecting long-tail threats, and static reward models ignore task difficulty.
Approach. DR-IRL uses inverse reinforcement learning for category-specific reward models, then enhances GRPO with dynamic reward scaling adjusting by task difficulty.

Keep the Best, Forget the Rest: Reliable Alignment with Order-Aware Preference Optimization

Problem. Direct Preference Optimization is sensitive to training sample quality, where ambiguous pairs from poorly aligned reference policies dominate gradients and degrade generalization.
Approach. RAPPO applies sample-aware modification to the DPO loss that filters out the hardest, most ambiguous samples while maintaining theoretical generalization guarantees.
Contribution. RAPPO achieves helpfulness of 0.693 (+34.8% over DPO) and harmlessness of 0.357 (-21.0% vs DPO) on the PKU-SafeRLHF benchmark.

Enforcing Axioms for AI Alignment under Loss-Based Rules

Problem. RLHF-based alignment methods can violate Pareto optimality, where a response may be less helpful and more toxic than another yet receive higher reward.
Approach. A linear social choice model is analyzed to show polynomial reward models cannot resolve axiom violations, but balanced dataset coverage via design enables loss-based rules to recover guarantees.
Contribution. The work provides a recipe for constitutional-style alignment with provable guarantees by enforcing balanced coverage in dataset design.

COMAL: A Convergent Meta-Algorithm for Aligning LLMs with General Preferences

Problem. Existing alignment methods rely on Bradley-Terry reward assumption which is insufficient to capture the complexity of general human preferences, particularly for LLM alignment.
Approach. Models alignment as a two-player zero-sum game with Nash equilibrium policy, proposes COMAL meta-algorithm inspired by convergent algorithms in game theory to find Nash policies.
Contribution. Converges to exact Nash policy in last iterate and maintains above 60.2% and 56.8% win rates on Llama-3-8B and Qwen2.5-7B against all compared algorithms.

P-GenRM: Personalized Generative Reward Model with Test-time User-based Scaling

Problem. Personalizing LLMs for individual user preferences faces challenges in obtaining accurate user-specific reward signals in open-ended scenarios, as existing models oversimplify preferences and struggle generalizing to new users with limited feedback.

Mitigating Mismatch within Reference-based Preference Optimization

Problem. Direct Preference Optimization's reliance on a reference policy introduces premature satisfaction failure where the policy margin merely beats reference margin even if the policy is still wrong on pessimistic pairs.
Approach. Hybrid-DPO (HyPO) applies reference conditionally as a drop-in modification: behaves like DPO when reference is optimistic or neutral, and treats reference as neutral when pessimistic by replacing Δθ-Δref with Δθ-max{0,Δref}.
Contribution. Strictly strengthens per-example learning signals on pessimistic pairs while preserving DPO's objective form and computational cost, improving inference performance across preference alignment.
